title: Review of c37's SH delay-map negative: Contradicted. The '-kap v' spot at kap 0.2, tau 10 drifts (8-10 body lengths by t=500, also in the parent's own probe_m2.png), and the Pyragas map used the stabilising sign; with kap<0 the spot drifts above |kap|tau ~ 1 and splits into a box-filling pattern at |kap|tau = 3
summary: Re-ran the claimed world (planted spot, N=128, L=80, b=2) with labkit on seeds 11-12 at the claimed settings and with a small seeded kick along a random direction (world_kick.py, KICK=0 is the original). The PYR=1 static spots replicate (kap 0.6, tau 10: 0 body lengths), but linear theory for the translation mode shows kap(v-u) with kap>0 is always stable; the Gurevich-Friedrich drift needs kap<0 with |kap|tau>1. With kap<0 the spot is static at |kap|tau 0.5-0.8, starts drifting at 1.2, drifts steadily at 1.5 (0.09/t, 11 body lengths by t=800, seeds 11, 12), and at 3 splits at t~70-85 into a hexagonal patch that fills the box and turns into a rotating spiral wave. The '-kap v' form at kap 0.2, tau 10 (kap*tau=2), which the finding lists as static, drifts from t~170 even without a kick (0.11/t, 8.3 body lengths by t=500), as the parent's probe_m2.png bottom row already shows. The finding's conclusion that these feedback forms give no splitting individuals stands in my runs (the only splitting is a front invasion), but its map is not a map of the drift bifurcation.

observations.M: rerun/claimed_inh_k02_t10/sheet.png: claimed '-kap v' kap 0.2, tau 10, no kick: spot leaves its site at t~170-215 and travels 8.3 body lengths by t=500 (FACTS.md, max speed 0.113/t)

seeds_run.result: fail: '-kap v' kap 0.2 tau 10 is not static (drifts 8.3 body lengths); PYR kap 0.6 tau 10 static as claimed
fail: same with a seeded kick (9.9 body lengths); PYR kap 0.6 static as claimed

controls_run.M: rerun/kick_inh_k02_t10 vs snap_m2.png (tau 2, kap*tau 0.4: static): drift only above kap*tau = 1; rerun/kick_pyr_kp06_t10 (kap>0 static) vs rerun/kick_pyr_km015_t10 (kap<0 drifts)

verdicts.limitation: The planted spot is deterministic, so seeds only change the kick direction. I did not test an exact delay buffer, other r, or longer runs at |kap|tau 1-3 where drifting spots might do more than invade. 'No splitting individuals' is not contradicted: at |kap|tau=3 the spot splits but the pieces invade the whole box as a pattern, which is not D. The parent's b is not recorded; I used b=2 (c39's value), the only b at which the spot exists here.
